title: Moon Phase Observation Station
subtitle: Why does the Moon look different on different nights?
coreQuestion: Does the Moon really change shape, or do we see different lit parts?
learningGoals: Know the Moon does not make light like the Sun.
Understand phases come from seeing different lit parts of the Moon.
Recognize common phases such as new, crescent, half, and full moon.
misconceptions: The Moon makes its own light.
The Moon really changes shape every day.
Moon phases are caused by Earth’s shadow every night.

hero.title: Moon Phase Observation Station
hero.lead: The Moon seems to change faces, but what changes is the lit part we see.
hero.sceneExplanation: The scene shows a gentle rooftop observation at night, an arc of Moon phases, and a simple Sun–Earth–Moon relationship diagram explaining where light comes from.
hero.childPrompt: Find the round Moon and the Moon with only a tiny bright edge.
hero.parentPrompt: Start with observing shapes, then guide the child toward lit parts and positions.

classificationGroups.name: Where light comes from
classificationGroups.childExplanation: The Sun lights the Moon, and the Moon reflects that light to us.
classificationGroups.parentNote: Say the Moon is like a reflecting friend.
classificationGroups.misconception: The Moon makes light like the Sun.

classificationGroups.name: Earth and Moon
classificationGroups.childExplanation: The Moon travels around Earth, and we look from Earth.
classificationGroups.misconception: The Moon just hangs still in the sky.

classificationGroups.name: Shapes we see
classificationGroups.childExplanation: We see curved, half, and round-looking Moons.
classificationGroups.parentNote: The visible shape is the lit part, not the Moon changing body.
classificationGroups.misconception: The Moon body grows and shrinks.

classificationGroups.name: Observation tools
classificationGroups.childExplanation: Eyes, windows, and telescopes can help us observe the Moon.
classificationGroups.misconception: You need a telescope to see Moon phases.

steps.childExplanation: The Sun always lights part of the Moon.
steps.parentNote: Set up the light source first.

steps.childExplanation: The Moon travels around Earth while sunlight hits it.
steps.parentNote: Focus on movement, not exact period.

steps.childExplanation: We can only see the side of the Moon facing us.
Sometimes we see a little, half, or all of the lit side.
steps.parentNote: Use a flashlight and ball demo.

steps.childExplanation: The phases change in order and repeat.
Try observing at about the same time each day.
Draw the bright part you see.
Check whether the Moon changed gradually.

clickTasks.title: Tap the Moon from thin to full
clickTasks.prompt: Start where it is barely visible and tap toward full Moon.
clickTasks.wrongHint: Start with the darkest, hardest-to-see Moon.
clickTasks.successCopy: You arranged part of the Moon’s journey toward full Moon.

clickTasks.title: Find: which one is the full Moon?
clickTasks.prompt: Find the roundest and brightest-looking Moon.
clickTasks.wrongHint: The full Moon has the whole visible face lit.
clickTasks.successCopy: Correct! That is the full Moon.

parentTips: Use a flashlight, a ball, and the child’s eyes to model Sun, Moon, and observer.
Do not begin with lunar eclipses; phases are not caused by Earth’s shadow every night.
Observing over several nights works better than explaining everything at once.

intro: The Moon looks as if it changes faces.
Actually, the Moon does not reshape itself; we see different lit parts.
keyFacts: From Earth, we see different amounts of the Moon’s lit side.
copy.explainPrompt: Can you use Sun, Earth, and Moon to explain Moon phases?

acceptanceCriteria: The child can say the Moon does not shine like the Sun by itself.
The child can identify at least three Moon phases.
The child can explain phases as different visible lit parts.

visualEvidenceBindings.observePrompt: Compare visual clues for Moonlight and Sunlight.
visualEvidenceBindings.evidenceCopy: Moonlight: soft-looking; reflected sunlight; does not warm Earth like the Sun. Sunlight: very bright; made by the Sun; brings light and heat. The Moon does not make light like the Sun.

visualEvidenceBindings.evidenceTitle: Shape changed vs Lit part changed
visualEvidenceBindings.observePrompt: Compare visual clues for Shape changed and Lit part changed.
visualEvidenceBindings.evidenceCopy: Shape changed: looks bitten; common mistake; the Moon body is not reshaping. Lit part changed: we see different bright parts; depends on Sun-Earth-Moon positions; forms the phase cycle. A phase is a different visible lit part.

visualEvidenceBindings.observePrompt: Compare visual clues for New Moon and Full Moon.
visualEvidenceBindings.evidenceCopy: New Moon: almost no bright side visible; not disappeared; still orbiting Earth. Full Moon: whole bright side visible; looks roundest; good for observing surface features. New and full Moon are the same Moon at different phases.
